prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” HVAC company for AC repair in Houston — the right choice depends on your location, budget, system type/age, and whether you need emergency service. That said, here’s a practical way to find the best company for your situation plus some reputable names you can start with.

How to pick a good HVAC company
- Check reviews: Google, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor, and the BBB for recent customer feedback.
- Verify credentials: ask for license and insurance (confirm license with the state or local regulator).
- Experience with your system: make sure they’ve repaired your brand/model and handle the system size of your home.
- Upfront pricing: get a written estimate that lists parts, labor, and warranties.
- Warranties: ask about parts and labor warranty length.
- Availability: do they offer 24/7 emergency service if you need it?
- Technician qualifications: NATE-certified techs are a good sign.
- Local vs national: local shops may offer personalized service; national chains may have better parts availability and consistent procedures.

Names commonly recommended in Houston (start here, then vet as above)
- John Moore Services — long-established, Houston-based company.
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (local branch) — large national network with local branches.
- Service Experts / One Hour / local independent shops — there are many reputable local family-owned HVAC shops in Houston.

Typical costs (ballpark)
- Diagnostic fee: $75–$150.
- Minor repairs (capacitor, contactor, sensor): $150–$600.
- Major repairs (compressor, refrigerant leak, condenser): $600–$2,000+.
(Prices vary with part cost, system age, and emergency service.)

Questions to ask when you call
- Are you licensed and insured? What’s your license number?
- Do you charge a diagnostic fee? Is it applied to the repair?
- What is the estimated cost range and timeline?
- What warranties do you offer on parts and labor?
- Are your techs NATE-certified or factory-trained for my brand?
- Can you provide recent references or reviews from local customers?

If you want, tell me your ZIP code and whether this is an emergency or a routine repair, and I can suggest a short list of highly rated companies in your area and what to ask them next.
